content:
Google announces new EmbeddingGemma 2 model that organizes, searches, and connects information directly on consumer hardware. To showcase its potential, Google developed a Mac app called AI Edge Foresight, featuring "smart notes."

EmbeddingGemma 2 "can help you find specific video clips from voice memos or search hours of audio recordings using text queries, all handled by a single, natively multimodal model."

This 7.4 billion parameter model is built on the Gemma 4 architecture and released as open source under the Apache 2.0 license. It is designed to operate locally in "resource-constrained environments":

For demonstration purposes, there are samples in the Google AI Edge Gallery (Android and iOS versions). A bigger demonstration is a brand-new Mac app called Google AI Edge Foresight.

During video conferences or in-person meetings, this note-taking app listens in the background, allowing you to "quickly jot down the key points you want to remember."

The app uses EmbeddingGemma 2 to "instantly combine these brief notes with meeting transcripts to enrich them into refined notes." Transcripts and audio are all processed locally on your device, not uploaded to the cloud.

Another feature allows you to "point Google AI Edge Foresight at your project folders, reference materials, charts, and calendars." Combined with local file and Google Drive support, users can ask the app questions and quickly obtain relevant information.

The chat feature offers "conversational retrieval and summarization of personal knowledge." There is also a Live Assistance feature that can "listen and automatically answer questions."

You can download Google AI Edge Foresight here. It joins two other Mac apps under Google: AI Edge Gallery and AI Edge Eloquent (offline transcription).
